content_voiceover: This continues the response criteria, now covering disease progression and relapse. Stable disease is not used as a formal response category, since time to progression better captures it. Progressive disease requires a twenty five percent increase from the lowest confirmed value, with an absolute serum M protein rise of at least zero point five grams per deciliter, or an absolute urine M protein rise of at least two hundred milligrams per day, along with alternatives for free light chains, bone marrow plasma cell percentage, new lesions, or a fifty percent increase in circulating plasma cells. Clinical relapse is a distinct, practical category requiring new CRAB features or organ dysfunction, new plasmacytomas or bone lesions, a definite fifty percent increase in existing lesion size, hypercalcemia over eleven, a hemoglobin drop of two grams per deciliter or more, a creatinine rise of two milligrams per deciliter or more, or hyperviscosity. Relapse from complete response or from MRD negative status requires reappearance of the M protein, five percent or more bone marrow plasma cells, or any new sign of progression such as a new plasmacytoma.
keypoints: Stable disease is not used as a formal response category; time-to-progression is preferred instead
Progressive disease: 25% relative increase from nadir with defined absolute thresholds in M protein, FLC, or marrow plasma cells
Progressive disease also includes new lesions or a 50% or more increase in circulating plasma cells
Clinical relapse: new CRAB features, new plasmacytomas, hypercalcemia, anemia, renal decline, or hyperviscosity
Relapse from CR or MRD-negative status: reappearing M protein, 5% or more marrow plasma cells, or a new progression sign
keypoint_voiceover: For exam purposes, remember progressive disease is a twenty five percent relative increase with a defined absolute threshold, half a gram per deciliter for serum M protein or two hundred milligrams a day for urine. Clinical relapse is the practical bedside category, driven by new CRAB features, new lesions, or hyperviscosity. And relapse from complete response or MRD negativity is confirmed by a reappearing M protein or five percent or more marrow plasma cells.
